title: The signed Hom complex of an additive bifunctor is exact on the homotopy category
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with countable products in $\mathcal C$ and a chosen derived category $D(\mathcal C)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $H:\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\to(\mathcal B\to\mathcal C)$ be a bifunctor additive separately in both variables, and fix an arbitrary cochain complex $I$ in $\mathcal B$. Define the signed Hom complex $\mathsf H_H(K,I)$ by $\mathsf H_H(K,I)^n=\prod_{p\in\mathbf Z}H(K^p,I^{p+n})$. With $\pi_{p,q}$ the projection to $H(K^p,I^q)$ for $q-p=n$, its differential from degree $n$ to $n+1$ is uniquely specified by
$$\pi_{p,q}\,d=(-1)^p\bigl(H(K^p,d_I)\,\pi_{p,q-1}-H(d_K,I^q)\,\pi_{p+1,q}\bigr),\qquad q-p=n+1,$$
where juxtaposition means composition in the displayed order of application, so the rightmost projection is applied first. Precomposition in $K$ gives a functor on its homotopy category, followed by localization in the target:
$$T_{H,I}:K(\mathcal A)^{\mathrm{op}}\longrightarrow D(\mathcal C),\qquad K\longmapsto Q_{\mathcal C}(\mathsf H_H(K,I)).$$
For this functor there is a coherent commutation with all integer shifts making it triangulated [def-weil-triangulated-category], with the opposite triangulation on the source. Both the shift structure and triangle maps refer to this signed differential (the upstream `CochainComplex.bifunctorHomObj` convention); in particular the underlying shift comparison identifies $\mathsf H_H(K[r],I)$ with $\mathsf H_H(K,I)[-r]$. No K-injectivity or acyclicity-preservation assumption on $I$ or on $H$ is required.

proof.text: Write $U(K)=\mathsf H_H(K,I)$. Construct its differential by the product universal property. On each projection, $d^2$ has two pure terms zero by $d_I^2=d_K^2=0$ and additivity; the mixed terms agree by bifunctor naturality and have coefficients $-(-1)^{2p}$ and $-(-1)^{2p+1}$, so cancel. Define $U(f)$ by componentwise precomposition. The chain-map equation follows from $f^{p+1}d=d f^p$ and naturality in the second variable. Identities, reversed composition and addition hold on every projection and hence on the products. This gives an additive contravariant functor on cochain complexes. All products are indexed by integers, so countable products suffice.

source.place: d_comp_d, bifunctorHomMapLeft, bifunctorHomMapLeft_id and bifunctorHomMapLeft_comp, lines 90-240; explicit projection calculation

proof.text: If $f,g:K\to L$ and $h^p:K^p\to L^{p-1}$ satisfy $f-g=d_Lh+hd_K$, define $v:U(L)^n\to U(K)^{n-1}$ by its $p$-th component $(-1)^pH(h^p,I^{p+n-1})\pi_{p-1,p+n-1}$. In $d_Uv+vd_U$, the two terms involving $d_I$ cancel, since their coefficients are $1$ and $-1$. The remaining terms at $p$ are precomposition by $h^{p+1}d_K^p+d_L^{p-1}h^p$, both with coefficient $1$, hence give $U(f)-U(g)$. Thus $U$ preserves homotopies. The homotopy-category quotient, whose arrows are chain maps modulo this relation, gives an additive functor $\bar U:K(\mathcal A)^{\mathrm{op}}\to K(\mathcal C)$. No quasi-isomorphism is used.

source.place: bifunctorHomMapLeftCochain and bifunctorHomMapLeftHomotopy, lines 242-304; explicit degree-minus-one formula

proof.text: For $r\in\mathbf Z$ put $b(r)=r(r+1)/2$, an integer. Define $s_{K,r}:U(K[r])\to U(K)[-r]$ by reindexing $j=p+r$ and multiplying the factor with original source index $p$ by $(-1)^{rp+b(r)}$. This is an isomorphism, with inverse given by the same sign and inverse reindexing. The postcomposition term of the source differential has coefficient $(-1)^p$; after reindexing the target coefficient is $(-1)^r(-1)^{p+r}=(-1)^p$. For the precomposition term the source additionally has $(-1)^r$ from $d_{K[r]}$; the multiplier at $p+1$ differs from that at $p$ by exactly $(-1)^r$. These are the two chain-map equations. Naturality follows from degreewise precomposition. The zero-shift map is the identity, and $b(r+s)=b(r)+b(s)+rs$ proves the addition law: the successive multiplier is $(-1)^{sp+b(s)+r(p+s)+b(r)}$. The equations remain true modulo homotopy. On the opposite source shift $[m]$, which is $[-m]$ on underlying complexes, use $s_{K,-m}$.

source.place: Tag 011G, definition-shift-cochain; agent computation for the signed differential

proof.text: Take a cone triangle $K\xrightarrow fL\xrightarrow iE\xrightarrow wK[1]$, with $w=-\pi$ as in [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. Its reversed triangle in the opposite category has vertices $E,L,K$ and third arrow represented contravariantly by $w[-1]:E[-1]\to K$. Put $X=U(L)$, $Y=U(K)$, $t=U(f)$. By [lem-sf-signed-bifunctor-cone-iso], $U(E)$ identifies with $\operatorname{Cone}(t)[-1]$ in coordinates $(y,x)$, differential $(-d_Yy-tx,d_Xx)$, and $U(i)$ becomes $(y,x)\mapsto x$. Compute the third arrow $Y\xrightarrow{U(w[-1])}U(E[-1])\xrightarrow{s_{E,-1}}U(E)[1]$. Its $E^j$ component on the $K^{j+1}$ summand is $(-1)^j$ times the input $Y$ component, because $w[-1]$ is minus projection and $s_{E,-1}$ contributes $(-1)^{j+1}$. Applying $\theta_f[1]$ multiplies that component by another $(-1)^j$; the result is $(y,x)=(\mathrm{id},0)$ into $\operatorname{Cone}(t)$. Thus all three arrows are exactly the inverse rotation of $X\xrightarrow tY\to\operatorname{Cone}(t)\xrightarrow{-\pi}X[1]$. That cone triangle is distinguished and inverse rotation is distinguished. Every distinguished triangle in the homotopy category is isomorphic to a cone triangle, so closure under triangle isomorphisms proves that $\bar U$, with the shifts of step 3, is triangulated.

source.place: Tag 08JC, lemma-RHom-triangulated, omitted cone-boundary calculation, supplied with the signed coordinate comparison

proof.text: By [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated], localization $Q_{\mathcal C}:K(\mathcal C)\to D(\mathcal C)$ is exact and commutes coherently with integer shifts. Compose it with $\bar U$. The resulting object and map formulas are precisely those of $T_{H,I}$. Its shift comparisons are $Q_{\mathcal C}(s)$ followed by the localization shift comparison; their zero and addition laws follow by functoriality from the two corresponding laws. A distinguished source triangle first goes to a distinguished triangle under $\bar U$ by step 4 and then to one under $Q_{\mathcal C}$. This proves the claimed exactness with the signed Hom model and the opposite source triangulation.
